records.name: Peru
records.summary_text:
Peru is a country that demands real caution for trans visitors, with a nationally-legislated bathroom ban and documented police violence, but no criminalisation of trans identity. The national legislature approved (February–April 2025) a bathroom ban prohibiting trans people from using public bathrooms matching their gender — a nationally-legislated restriction comparable to bans passed in other countries. A consumer-protection body dismissed a trans woman's discrimination complaint against a gym that enforced the policy.

records.name: Uruguay
records.summary_text:
Uruguay is one of Latin America's safest and most progressive destinations for trans visitors. The Comprehensive Law for Trans People (Law 19,684, 2018) provides legal gender recognition by administrative self-declaration (no surgery or diagnosis required), a reparation pension for trans victims of institutional violence, and a state employment quota for trans people. Same-sex marriage has been legal since 2013 (Latin America's first), and bathroom access is legally protected.
